_meta.note: Static reference values entered from the NASA fact sheets; not re-fetched on 2026-10-12. Gravity = mean equatorial surface gravity (m/s²); for the gas/ice giants, at the 1-bar level. Diameters are equatorial.
_meta.layout_warning: The 3D layout uses a compressed, non-linear VISUALISATION scale. It is not a physically accurate distance or size map.

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.atmosphere: Hot plasma; outer layers are the photosphere, chromosphere and corona.
bodies.summary: The star at the centre of the Solar System, holding over 99% of its mass.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.summary: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.summary: Similar in size to Earth, with a runaway greenhouse atmosphere.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.summary: Our home planet, orbited by the Moon.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.summary: A cold desert world with the largest volcano in the Solar System.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.summary: The largest planet, with a persistent giant storm, the Great Red Spot.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.summary: Known for its extensive ring system.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.summary: An ice giant rotating on its side.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.summary: The outermost recognised planet, with supersonic winds.

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.atmosphere: Essentially none; an extremely thin exosphere.
bodies.summary: Earth's only natural satellite and the destination of the CLPS programme.
